payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Was the specific black DVD in the source image transformed into a visibly white DVD in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass only if the source black DVD can be matched to an edited object and that same object is visibly white while remaining identifiable as a DVD. Fail if the source DVD is confidently matched and remains black, or is confidently shown not to have been transformed into a white DVD. Unknown if the source DVD's identity or correspondence to an edited object cannot be established.
node.binding: Compare the small rectangular item near the center of the source with both edited white discs. Weigh position, shape, and surrounding scene context together; do not assume either disc is the source DVD based on whiteness or location alone. Judge only whether the requested transformation is established, not whether some unrelated white disc appeared. Reserve unknown for genuinely unresolved source identity or correspondence.

node_traces.evidence: The source has a small rectangular, apparently black/gray item near the center. In the edited image there are two white discs: one near the center-left and one beside the dark object on the right. The source item’s rectangular appearance and the changed scene make its correspondence to either disc unclear; neither can be confidently identified as the transformed DVD.

d2: The trace’s uncertainty is about correspondence, not whether the requested edit progressed: the source’s small rectangular DVD case/cover near the center is replaced by a white disc in roughly the same location, while the other white disc lies by the dark object at right. The binding already says to compare position, shape, and context, but its broad “confidently matched” criterion may let the model stop at shape mismatch without weighing the strong positional/contextual cue. Clarify how to assess a plausible transformed match when the edit changes an object’s appearance, and require an explicit comparison of each candidate and its location before resolving identity. Keep whiteness alone insufficient and do not turn this identity check into a color-progress judgment. The reference “no” is an aggregate outcome, not atomic proof that either disc is the source item; preserve uncertainty if correspondence genuinely remains unresolved. The trace is valid and queried with no dependency or transport failure, so focus on visual reasoning and criterion calibration rather than execution plumbing.
